rules.title: Plastered strawbale braced wall panels in one-story buildings shall comply with R602.10 and Tables AS106.13(1)-(3)
rules.intent: Ensure plastered strawbale walls used as lateral bracing meet the same wall-bracing framework as conventional wood-frame construction with thickness, sill plate, and anchor-bolt detailing tuned to plastered bale assemblies.
evidence_required: Bracing schedule identifying each strawbale panel by Type (A1-E) per Table AS106.13(1)
Detail showing minimum 15-inch unplastered bale thickness
Sill-plate anchor bolt schedule (5/8" dia., 7" embed., 3x3x3/16 washer) at the spacing shown in Table AS106.13(1)
Wind/seismic site-criteria summary referencing Section R301.2.1 and R301.2.2
Approved engineered design where the building is in a special wind region or where wind design is required per Figure R301.2(2)

rules.title: Cob braced wall panels shall comply with R602.10 and Tables AU106.11(1)-(5) with prescribed wind/seismic criteria
rules.intent: Bring monolithic-adobe (cob) walls used for lateral bracing into the prescriptive wall-bracing system with cob-specific tables for panel types, spacing and length.
evidence_required: Bracing plan identifying each cob panel by Type per Table AU106.11(1)
Spacing and length tables (AU106.11(2)-(5)) cross-referenced for wind and seismic design
Approved engineered design where in special wind region or where wind design is required per Figure R301.2.1.1
Wind/seismic site criteria summary
Reinforcement and anchorage details for each cob panel type

rules.title: Design wind loads using the ultimate design wind speed from Figure R301.2(2) and provide a continuous load path
rules.intent: Establish the wind loading basis (Vult from Figure R301.2(2), exposure adjustments) and require a continuous uplift load path so wind forces transfer from roof to foundation.

requires.lowest_prescriptive_speed_floor: Where Vult < lowest prescriptive code wind speed, use the lowest prescriptive code wind speed

exceptions.note: Where wind design is required per R301.2.1.1, the prescriptive structural wind provisions of this code are not permitted.

evidence_required: Site-specific Vult from Figure R301.2(2) with citation
Exposure category determination per R301.2.1.4
Wall covering / glazing / roof covering wind pressures from Table R301.2.1(1) adjusted by Table R301.2.1(2)
Continuous uplift load path detail from roof to foundation per Section R802.11
Statement that prescriptive lowest wind speed is used where Vult is below the lowest tabulated value

rules.title: Apply IRC seismic provisions to townhouses and dwellings in SDC C/D0/D1/D2; SDC E uses the California Building Code
rules.intent: Define which buildings are bound by the IRC seismic provisions and require engineered (CBC) design for SDC E unless reclassified.
evidence_required: Seismic Design Category determination per Section R301.2.2.1
Identification of building type (detached 1-2 family dwelling vs. townhouse)
If SDC E: engineered design per California Building Code or reclassification documentation per R301.2.2.1.2
Statement that seismic provisions of this code are applied

rules.title: Assign Seismic Design Category from Figures R301.2.2.1(1) through (6)
rules.intent: Force every IRC project to obtain its SDC from the prescribed maps before any other seismic provision applies.

alternate_methods_permitted: Section R301.2.2.1.1 (Site Class A, B, or D using Figures R301.2.2.1.1(1)-(6) or CBC 1613.2)
Section R301.2.2.1.2 (Reclassify SDC E to D2 under stated restrictions)

evidence_required: Site coordinates with mapped SDC pulled from the applicable Figure R301.2.2.1(1)-(6)
If alternate method used: site class report and SDS calculation per CBC 1613.2 with SDC from Table R301.2.2.1.1
If reclassifying SDC E to D2: documentation under R301.2.2.1.2 including R301.2.2.6 regularity check

rules.title: Irregular buildings in SDC C/D0/D1/D2 shall not use IRC seismic provisions; design per accepted engineering practice
rules.intent: Prevent prescriptive seismic provisions from being applied to plan/configuration irregularities they were not calibrated for; require engineering for the irregular feature and any forces it generates.

exceptions.note: Subject to all five conditions of the R301.2.2.6 Item 1 exception (joist size/spacing, backspan ratio, doubled joists, rim-joist tie, gravity load limits).

evidence_required: Plan and elevation showing whether any of the eight irregularity conditions of R301.2.2.6 occur
Engineered design (calculations and details) for the irregular feature and remaining system if applicable
Hillside-construction structural design for floor above cripple walls and connections down to and including the foundation, if Item 8 applies

rules.title: In SDC D0/D1/D2 support exterior walls (and required interior braced wall panels in long buildings) on continuous footings
rules.intent: Provide a continuous, stiff foundation diaphragm in higher seismic categories so braced wall panel forces transfer reliably to the soil.

requires.engineered_alternative: Other footing materials or systems shall be designed in accordance with accepted engineering practice.

evidence_required: Foundation plan showing continuous concrete or fully-grouted masonry footings under exterior walls
Plan dimensions noted to confirm whether interior braced wall panels require continuous footings (>50 ft trigger)
Two-story SDC D2 confirmation that all braced wall panels (interior and exterior) sit on continuous foundations
If exception is used: cripple-wall height, first-floor support detail, and bracing-line spacing dimensioned on plans

rules.title: Reinforce footings and stem walls in SDC D0/D1/D2 per Section R403.1.3 and Figure R403.1.3
rules.intent: Add minimum reinforcement to concrete footings and stem walls so the foundation behaves as a ductile, continuous element under seismic demand.

subsections_apply: R403.1.3.1 concrete stem walls with concrete footings
R403.1.3.2 masonry stem walls with concrete footings
R403.1.3.4 interior bearing and braced wall panel footings

evidence_required: Foundation reinforcement schedule and section details consistent with Figure R403.1.3
Reinforcement size, lap-splice length and cover dimensions per R403.1.3.5
Compressive strength of concrete (f'c) called out per Table R402.2
Hooked dowels into stem walls per R403.1.3.1/2 and turned-down footing detail per R403.1.3.3 where applicable

rules.title: In SDC C (townhouses) and SDC D0/D1/D2 add plate washers, tighter interior anchor-bolt spacing, and 4-ft anchor spacing >2 stories
rules.intent: Provide hold-down-grade sill anchorage so braced wall panel sills transfer seismic shear to the foundation without splitting and so multi-story buildings get extra anchor density.
evidence_required: Anchor-bolt schedule with plate washers (3x3x0.229) called out along all required braced wall lines
Foundation plan showing interior braced wall and bearing-wall anchor bolt spacing <= 6 ft (or 4 ft if >2 stories) and within 12 in. of plate ends
Stepped cripple wall detail per R602.11.2 if applicable
Force-transfer detail at continuous wood foundations matching R602.11.1 capacity

rules.title: Foundation walls in SDC D0/D1/D2: limit height/backfill, set minimum thicknesses, and add prescribed reinforcement
rules.intent: Cap unreinforced foundation-wall demand and require minimum reinforcement so plain masonry/concrete walls do not become brittle weak links in higher seismic categories.
evidence_required: Foundation wall section showing height <= 8 ft and unbalanced backfill <= 4 ft, or applicable engineered design table reference
Reinforcement schedule (No. 4 vertical at <= 48" o.c., two No. 4 horizontal in top 12 in.) for masonry walls
Concrete-wall thickness >= 7.5 in. (or 6 in. with wall height <= 4'-6")
Vertical/horizontal bar layout per Table R404.1.2 where plain concrete is used outside limits

rules.title: Size floor joists from Tables R502.3.1(1) and R502.3.1(2) (or AWC STJR for other species/loads)
rules.intent: Bound the gravity-load span of floor joists prescriptively so floor diaphragms remain stiff enough to transfer lateral loads to the bracing system.
evidence_required: Floor framing plan calling out joist size, species, grade and spacing
Span table reference (R502.3.1(1) for sleeping/attic, R502.3.1(2) for living areas)
Live/dead load assumptions noted on plans (e.g., 30 psf LL, 20 psf DL for sleeping areas)
If species/loads are outside the table: AWC STJR calculation

rules.title: Restrain joists against rotation at supports and (in SDC D0-D2) at each intermediate support
rules.intent: Keep floor joists from rolling or twisting where they bear so the floor diaphragm and braced wall panel-to-floor connection stay effective.
evidence_required: Detail showing solid blocking, rim/band joist or stud attachment at each joist end
If SDC D0/D1/D2: blocking detail at every intermediate support
Manufacturer's lateral-bracing instructions for trusses, SCL, glulam or I-joists
Floor framing plan note referencing R502.7

rules.title: Brace buildings per Section R602.10 (or R602.12 simplified bracing where applicable); engineer non-conforming portions
rules.intent: Make wall bracing the primary lateral system for IRC buildings and require engineering wherever the prescriptive rules cannot be met.
evidence_required: Bracing plan citing Section R602.10 (or R602.12 simplified bracing) on each story
List of any wall lines designed per Section R301.1 instead of R602.10
Engineer-of-record stamp for any portion that does not comply with R602.10

rules.title: Designate braced wall lines as straight lines in plan, with offsets <= 4 ft from the designated line
rules.intent: Force the bracing geometry to be discretized into well-defined orthogonal lines so the prescriptive bracing tables and panel-location rules can be applied unambiguously.
evidence_required: Bracing plan with braced wall lines drawn as straight lines and labeled
Dimensions showing all panel offsets <= 4 ft from designated lines
Calculation that no more than 2/3 of required braced wall panel length lies on one side of any line
Identification of braced wall line ends per Figure R602.10.1.1

rules.title: Space parallel braced wall lines per Table R602.10.1.3 (60 ft wind; 35 ft SDC C townhouse; 25 ft SDC D0-D2)
rules.intent: Cap the diaphragm span between bracing lines so floor and roof diaphragms can deliver wind and seismic loads to the bracing without excessive flexibility.
evidence_required: Bracing plan with parallel braced wall line spacing dimensioned
Vult, SDC and building type shown to confirm correct row of Table R602.10.1.3
If exception used: documented adjustment per Table R602.10.3(4)
Single-room area calculation if 35-ft spacing exception is invoked in SDC D0-D2

rules.title: Build braced wall panels as full-height segments without offsets and place them per Section R602.10
rules.intent: Guarantee each braced wall panel is a continuous full-height shear element so the prescriptive lengths and capacities apply.
evidence_required: Wall elevations showing each braced wall panel from top plate to bottom plate without offsets
Bracing plan citing Section R602.10.4 method for each panel
Confirmation that panel placement complies with R602.10.2.2 / R602.10.2.2.1

rules.title: Compute required length of bracing along each braced wall line from Tables R602.10.3(1)/(3) with adjustment factors (2)/(4)
rules.intent: Make the design length of bracing a deterministic function of wind speed, SDC, story, building geometry and adjustment factors so plan checkers can re-derive it from the plans.
evidence_required: Per-line bracing calculation showing Vult, SDC, story, line spacing and required length from Table R602.10.3(1) and/or (3)
Adjustment factors from Table R602.10.3(2) and/or (4) applied (e.g., wall height, mean roof height, eave-to-ridge, gypsum, blocking)
Tally of provided bracing length per line vs. required
If angled walls used: projected length calculation per Figure R602.10.1.4

rules.title: Construct intermittent and continuously sheathed braced wall panels per Table R602.10.4
rules.intent: Bind each prescriptive method (LIB, DWB, WSP, SFB, GB, PBS, PCP, HPS, ABW, PFH, PFG, BV-WSP, CS-WSP, CS-G, CS-PF, CS-SFB) to a specific material, thickness and fastening so the assumed lateral capacity is realized.
evidence_required: Method label for each panel cross-referenced to Table R602.10.4 row
Sheathing/material thickness, fastener type and spacing on the wall details
Notes prohibiting adhesive attachment in SDC C, D0, D1 and D2 (per Table R602.10.4 note a)

rules.title: Mix bracing methods only as Section R602.10.4.1 permits, using the highest required length when mixing within a wall line
rules.intent: Allow practical mixing of bracing methods without diluting the required total bracing length; cap mixing within a single wall line to lower-seismic conditions.
evidence_required: Bracing plan annotating which methods are mixed and at what level (story, line, or along a line)
Bracing-length calculation using the highest required length when mixing along a line
SDC and Vult shown to confirm mixing scenario is permitted
R602.10.7 end conditions shown for any continuously sheathed segment

rules.title: Continuous sheathing methods require structural panels on every sheathable surface of one side of the wall line
rules.intent: Make 'continuous sheathing' literal: the entire one-sided sheathing field (above/below openings and gable ends) acts as the bracing system, so end conditions and length tables can rely on it.
evidence_required: Wall elevations showing structural sheathing on all sheathable areas (above/below openings, gable ends) along the continuously sheathed wall line
Cross-reference to Section R602.10.7 end-condition figure for each end of the line
Method (CS-WSP, CS-G, CS-PF or CS-SFB) called out per panel

rules.title: In SDC D0-D2 with stone/masonry veneer per R703.8, brace exterior and supporting interior walls per Section R602.10.6.5
rules.intent: Account for the extra mass and overturning that veneer adds in higher seismic categories by triggering Method BV-WSP, hold-down rules and continuous-foundation requirements.
evidence_required: Plan note identifying veneer extent (first story only / exceeds first story / limited per R602.10.6.5.3)
Method BV-WSP details (Figure R602.10.6.5.2) where veneer exceeds first story height
Hold-down schedule per Table R602.10.6.5.4
If townhouse with veneer exceeds first story or 1-2 family in D2 exceeds two stories: engineered design
Confirmation that no cripple walls exist where veneer exceeds first-story height

rules.title: Each end of a continuously sheathed braced wall line shall match one of the conditions in Figure R602.10.7
rules.intent: Provide a defined corner detail (return panel, hold-down, or full-height return) at the end of a continuous-sheathing line so the line can develop the assumed lateral capacity.
evidence_required: Each end of every continuously sheathed line detailed per Figure R602.10.7 (one of End Conditions 1-5)
If End Condition 4: 24-inch return panel applied to each side of the corner
If End Condition 5: 1,800-lb hold-down at the panel-end stud and to foundation/framing below

rules.title: In SDC D0-D2 fasten braced wall panels to required foundations per R602.11.1 and use 8-16d top plate splice
rules.intent: Tie braced wall panels into the foundation with the higher-seismic anchorage and preserve top plate continuity to act as a chord/collector.
evidence_required: Foundation anchorage detail at each braced wall panel matching R602.11.1 (plate washers, anchor bolts)
Top-plate splice detail showing 8-16d face nails on each side of the splice
Bracing plan note pointing to R602.10.8.1 in SDC D0/D1/D2

rules.title: Support braced wall panels on cantilevered joists, post/pier, or stem walls only as R602.10.9 permits
rules.intent: Restrict the kinds of substructure that can carry a braced wall panel so the panel's overturning and shear can be resisted by the supporting element.
evidence_required: Foundation/floor-framing detail at each braced wall panel matching one of the permitted support types
Engineered design for raised-floor post/pier supports
Reinforcement schedule per Figure R602.10.9 for short masonry/concrete stem walls
Statement that ABW and PFH panels are not attached to masonry stem walls

rules.title: In SDC D0-D2 braced wall panel footings shall meet Section R403.1.2
rules.intent: Force the higher-seismic continuous-foundation rule to the panel level so each braced wall panel sits on a continuous concrete or fully grouted masonry footing.
evidence_required: Foundation plan showing every required braced wall panel supported on a continuous footing complying with R403.1.2
Plan note linking R602.10.9.1 to the foundation plan
Documentation of any R403.1.2 exception used (two-story with cripple wall <= 4 ft, etc.)

rules.title: Brace cripple walls with the same length and method as the wall above, multiplied by 1.15
rules.intent: Compensate for the soft-story potential of cripple walls by increasing the bracing demand 15% above what the wall above requires.
evidence_required: Cripple wall bracing calculation showing wall-above method and length multiplied by 1.15
Adjustment factors applied per Tables R602.10.3(2)/(4)
If gypsum board is omitted on the inside of the cripple wall, the gypsum-elimination factor is also applied
Cripple wall framing detail per R602.9 (stud size and continuous foundation support)

rules.title: In SDC D0/D1 (and SDC C townhouses) limit cripple wall bracing to WSP/CS-WSP with 14-ft max panel spacing
rules.intent: Restrict cripple-wall bracing to the most reliable wood-structural-panel methods and tighten panel spacing where the soft-story risk is highest.
evidence_required: Cripple wall plan limiting methods to WSP or CS-WSP
Dimensioned spacing showing distance between adjacent panel edges <= 14 ft
If interior braced wall line not on continuous foundation: parallel cripple wall bracing length increased by 1.5
If 4-in. edge nailing used: 0.7 length factor and engineered design fallback noted

rules.title: Anchor braced wall line sills to concrete or masonry foundations per R403.1.6 and R602.11.1
rules.intent: Make sill anchorage to the foundation an explicit, named requirement at every braced wall line sill so it is not skipped by reference only.
evidence_required: Anchor-bolt schedule along every braced wall line sill citing R403.1.6 (size, spacing, embedment) and R602.11.1 (plate washer)
Foundation plan showing each sill with anchor bolts dimensioned
Plate washer note (3x3x0.229 in.) at each anchor bolt

rules.title: In SDC D0-D2 (and SDC C townhouses) provide 0.229 x 3 x 3 plate washers at all sill anchor bolts (slotted hole permitted within limits)
rules.intent: Spread the anchor-bolt clamp force across the sill plate so it does not split or shear, and allow practical slotted holes only within strict size limits.
evidence_required: Hardware schedule listing 3x3x0.229 plate washers (or approved anchor straps) at every required braced wall line anchor
Detail showing slot dimensions <= bolt+3/16" wide and <= 1-3/4" long with cut washer above plate washer
Plan note linking R602.11.1 to the SDC of the project
Manufacturer spec sheet for anchor straps if used as alternative

rules.title: In SDC D0-D2 stepped-foundation braced wall lines shall follow the three R602.11.2 cases
rules.intent: Provide explicit prescriptive details for the difficult stepped-foundation condition so the line above the step still functions as a braced wall line.
evidence_required: Foundation step detail labeled as Case 1, 2 or 3 of R602.11.2 (matching Figure R602.11.2)
Top plate splice and anchor-bolt placement (within 1 ft and 3 ft of step) for Case 1
Cripple-wall bracing calculation per R602.10.10/.1/.2 for Case 2
R403.1.6 and R602.11.1 anchorage detail for Case 3

rules.title: Use simplified wall bracing only when all eight R602.12 prerequisites are satisfied
rules.intent: Restrict the simplified bracing alternative to small, low-wind, low-seismic, regular buildings where the simplified rectangle method is reliable.
evidence_required: Eligibility checklist confirming all eight R602.12 conditions
Vult and exposure category from Figure R301.2(2) and R301.2.1.4
SDC determination from R301.2.2.1
Circumscribed-rectangle diagram per R602.12.1 (max 60 ft side, max 3:1 aspect ratio)
Statement that other R602.10 bracing provisions are not used (except as expressly cited in R602.12)

rules.title: Provide a braced wall panel uplift load path at exterior walls supporting roof framing per one of three options
rules.intent: Guarantee that wind uplift at the roof reaches the foundation by either fastening per Table R602.3(1) within stated limits, dedicated uplift connectors, or engineered combined uplift/shear sheathing.
evidence_required: Uplift calculation per Section R802.11 at the top of each exterior wall supporting roof framing
If Option 1: documentation of Vult, exposure, roof pitch and span limits
If Option 2: hold-down/strap schedule from top plate to foundation with continuous load path
If Option 3: engineer's combined uplift+shear sheathing/fastener calculation

rules.title: Frame cripple walls with studs sized for an additional story when over 4 ft tall, sheathe short cripple walls, and support all on continuous foundations
rules.intent: Treat cripple walls as a real (potentially extra) story for stud sizing, and require continuous sheathing or solid blocking at very short cripple walls so they do not become a soft band.
evidence_required: Cripple wall framing detail showing stud size (and a story increase if height > 4 ft)
Solid blocking or WSP-sheathed detail when stud height < 14 in.
Foundation plan showing continuous foundation under all cripple walls
Cripple-wall height dimension on building section

rules.title: Install cold-formed steel structural sheathing on all sheathable exterior wall surfaces per Figure R603.9
rules.intent: Make CFS structural sheathing continuous (including above and below openings) so the wall acts as a single shear element analogous to wood continuous sheathing.
evidence_required: CFS wall elevation showing structural sheathing on every sheathable surface (including above/below openings)
Sheathing material spec (>= 7/16 in. OSB or 15/32 in. plywood)
Fastening pattern matching Figure R603.9 and Table R603.3.2(1)
Reference to AISI S230 prescriptive method

rules.title: Determine minimum length of full-height CFS sheathing from Tables R603.9.2(1) and R603.9.2(2), with 20% floor
rules.intent: Compute a CFS-specific bracing length tied to wind speed/exposure, roof slope, story location and plan aspect ratio, while floor-stopping at 20% of line length so very short bracing is impossible.
evidence_required: Per-line CFS bracing calculation: line length × Table R603.9.2(1) percentage × Table R603.9.2(2) factor
Confirmation that minimum percentage >= 20% of line length
Wall-height factor (1.10 for 9-ft, 1.20 for 10-ft) applied as appropriate
Hold-down anchors per R603.9.4.2 if 0.6 lowest-story factor is used
48-in. corner panels and blocking detail (>= 33 mil) per Item 2 where applicable

rules.title: CFS walls with stone/masonry veneer per R703.8: determine sheathing length per R603.9.5 (per SDC)
rules.intent: Account for veneer mass and overturning when computing CFS sheathing length and overturning anchorage, varying the rule by SDC.
evidence_required: Identification of all walls 'backing or perpendicular to and laterally supporting' veneered walls
If SDC C: greater length of R603.9.2 (R603.9.2.2 still permitted)
If SDC D0/D1/D2: length and overturning anchor schedule from Tables R603.9.5(1)-(4)
Hold-down detail at doubled studs at the end of each full-height wall segment

rules.title: Construct buildings to the climatic and geographic design criteria established for the jurisdiction in Table R301.2
rules.intent: Anchor every structural design parameter (wind speed, seismic design category, frost line depth, flood hazard, ground snow, weathering, termite, etc.) to the values the local jurisdiction has filled in on Table R301.2 so the prescriptive provisions of the code are applied with the correct site conditions.
evidence_required: Title sheet or general notes listing the Table R301.2 values (wind, seismic, frost, termite, flood, snow) for the project address
Citation of the source figures (Figures R301.2(1)-(4), R301.2.1.1, R403.3(2), R318.4) used to establish each value
Geotechnical or jurisdictional letter confirming values where the jurisdiction has not pre-filled the table

rules.title: Use naturally durable wood or AWPA U1 preservative-treated wood at all locations exposed to decay
rules.intent: Prevent rot and structural failure of wood members in contact with concrete, masonry, the ground, or weather by requiring decay-resistant material at the eight specifically called-out exposure conditions.
evidence_required: Foundation/framing plans showing clearances of wood members from grade and concrete contact
Wood species/grade and treatment specification (AWPA U1) on the structural notes
Quality mark / treatment label on lumber per Section R317.2
Detail showing pier or metal pedestal with moisture barrier for any wood column in contact with basement floor

rules.title: In termite-prone areas, protect the structure by one or a combination of the six accepted termite-control methods
rules.intent: Prevent subterranean termite damage in jurisdictions identified as termite-risk areas on Table R301.2 by requiring at least one approved control method.
evidence_required: Termite designation from the jurisdiction's Table R301.2 entry
Specification on plans of the selected method(s) (chemical product, bait system, treated lumber, barrier detail, or steel framing schedule)
Manufacturer label/data sheet for any baiting system or physical barrier used
Treatment certificate for chemical termiticide work

rules.title: Design and construct buildings in flood hazard areas per Section R322 (or ASCE 24)
rules.intent: Make sure any building in whole or part within a flood hazard area is designed, anchored, elevated, materially specified and detailed to resist flotation, collapse, lateral movement, and water damage from the design flood.

exceptions.note: ASCE 24 may be used in lieu of Section R322 subject to the limits of both.

evidence_required: Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panel and base flood elevation for the site
Elevation Certificate prepared and sealed by a registered design professional documenting the as-built lowest-floor elevation
Foundation, flood-opening and break-away wall details per Section R322.2 or R322.3
Specification list of flood-damage-resistant materials below the DFE referencing FEMA TB-2
Anchorage calculation for any underground or above-ground tank

rules.title: Scope: Chapter 4 controls foundation design and construction; foundations in flood hazard areas must also meet R322
rules.intent: Establish the trigger for the entire foundation rule pack and require Section R322 compliance whenever the site is in a flood hazard area.
evidence_required: Foundation plan and details referencing the Chapter 4 prescriptive section used (R403, R404, etc.)
If wood foundations: AWC PWF design package
Flood-zone determination on title sheet and cross-reference to Section R322 where applicable

rules.title: Limit prescriptive wood foundations to two-story buildings with interior walls at ≤50 ft and engineer them in SDC D0/D1/D2
rules.intent: Bound the use of prescriptive wood foundations to building configurations the code's tabulated limits actually cover, and require engineering when seismic demand is high.
evidence_required: Foundation plan showing building has ≤2 floors and a roof, with interior basement/foundation walls at ≤50 ft on center
Seismic Design Category from Table R301.2 on the title sheet
If SDC D0/D1/D2: stamped engineering calculations for the wood foundation

rules.title: Provide concrete with the minimum f'c from Table R402.2 and air-entrain it where the weathering potential is moderate or severe
rules.intent: Match concrete strength and air entrainment to the freeze-thaw and exposure environment so foundations, slabs and exterior flatwork do not spall or fail in service.
evidence_required: Concrete mix design submittal listing f'c, air content, and SCM percentages
Weathering index taken from Figure R301.2(1) / Table R301.2 cited on plans
Batch tickets and 28-day compressive-strength test reports per ASTM C39
Where air entrainment is required: confirmation of total air content within 5–7% (or 3% min for steel-troweled garage floors at f'c ≥4000 psi)

rules.title: Support all exterior walls on continuous footings (concrete, fully-grouted masonry, crushed stone, wood, or other approved system) sized for the loads
rules.intent: Ensure every exterior wall has a continuous load path to undisturbed soil or engineered fill, designed by Section R403 or ACI 332.
evidence_required: Foundation plan showing continuous footing under every exterior wall
Allowable soil-bearing value (Section R401.4 / Table R401.4.1 or geotechnical report) called out on plans
Section detail showing footing on undisturbed soil or engineered fill
Calculations or table reference establishing footing width and thickness

rules.title: Place exterior footings at least 12 inches below undisturbed grade (and to frost depth where applicable)
rules.intent: Keep footings below seasonal soil-disturbance depth and out of frost-heave zones.
evidence_required: Foundation section detail dimensioning footing bottom ≥12 in below undisturbed grade
Frost-line depth from Table R301.2 cited and shown on detail
Soils report or note that footing bears on undisturbed natural soil or engineered fill

rules.title: Protect foundation walls, piers and other permanent supports from frost by one of four approved methods
rules.intent: Eliminate frost-heave damage by extending footings below the frost line, using a frost-protected shallow foundation, designing per ASCE 32, or founding on solid rock.
evidence_required: Frost-line depth from Table R301.2 on the title sheet
Foundation section detail showing footing bottom at or below the frost line, OR FPSF detail per R403.3, OR ASCE 32 stamped design, OR rock-bearing detail
Soils note prohibiting placement on frozen soil

rules.title: Frost-protected shallow foundations are allowed only for heated buildings (≥64°F monthly mean) per Figure R403.3(1) and Table R403.3(1)
rules.intent: Allow shallow foundations in cold climates only where building heat keeps the soil from freezing, and require ASTM C578-labeled below-grade insulation to provide that thermal envelope.
evidence_required: Mechanical schedule confirming building is heated to monthly mean ≥64°F
Foundation detail matching Figure R403.3(1) with vertical and horizontal insulation dimensioned
Insulation product data sheet showing ASTM C578 compliance and the R-value and thickness from Table R403.3(1)
Air-Freezing Index for the site from Figure R403.3(2) or Table R403.3(2)

rules.title: Select and design concrete or masonry foundation walls per R404.1.2/R404.1.3; engineer walls under hydrostatic head or >48 in unbalanced backfill
rules.intent: Route foundation walls into either the prescriptive tables or accepted engineering practice depending on the height of unbalanced backfill and the presence of groundwater.
evidence_required: Foundation wall reinforcing plan and section keyed to Tables R404.1.1, R404.1.2(1)–(8) (and R404.1.2(9) for flat basement walls)
Soils report stating groundwater elevation and backfill height
Where groundwater or unbalanced backfill >48 in: engineer's stamped calculations for the wall
Lateral support detail at top and bottom of wall

rules.title: In flood hazard areas, provide flood openings in under-floor walls and place finished ground level under-floor at or above outside grade on at least one side
rules.intent: Equalize hydrostatic pressure on under-floor enclosure walls and ensure under-floor space drains to grade so foundation walls are not blown out by floodwaters.
evidence_required: Foundation plan showing flood opening locations, sizes, and bottom-of-opening elevations meeting R322.2.2
Site/grading plan demonstrating interior under-floor finished grade is ≥ outside finished grade on at least one side
FEMA TB 11-1 compliance documentation if relying on the exception

rules.title: Cold-formed steel floor framing must be cold-formed from structural-quality sheet steel meeting AISI S240 Section A3
rules.intent: Guarantee that load-bearing CFS floor members are produced from structural-grade material with documented mechanical properties.
evidence_required: Mill certificate or AISI S240 product identification mark on each CFS floor member
Structural notes citing AISI S240 Section A3 for material
Member schedule listing dimensions, thickness and material grade per AISI S230 Section A4.3/A4.4

rules.title: Support decks on concrete footings (or other approved system) sized for the imposed loads
rules.intent: Transfer all gravity, live and lateral loads from elevated decks to ground via footings of correct size, depth and frost protection.
evidence_required: Deck plan showing footing locations and tributary areas
Footing schedule sized from Table R507.3.1 against allowable soil-bearing pressure (Table R401.4.1)
Section showing footing ≥12 in below undisturbed grade and frost-line compliance
Where attached to a frost-protected structure: detail of the frost-protection method

rules.title: Scope: Chapter 6 controls wall and partition design and construction; walls must transmit loads to supports
rules.intent: Anchor every wall-construction rule to the load-path requirement of Section R301 so wind, seismic, gravity and lateral loads reach the foundation through compliant assemblies.
evidence_required: Structural drawings showing each wall framing system and supporting element
Load path diagram from roof to foundation
Reference to Section R301 design loads on title sheet

rules.title: Use only conforming wood products and grades for load-bearing wood wall framing
rules.intent: Make sure every load-supporting wood element in a wood-framed wall has documented structural properties from a recognized standard or grading agency.
evidence_required: Lumber grade marks on framing or certification of inspection
Structural notes specifying species, grade and stud size/spacing per Table R602.3(5)
Fastening schedule referencing Tables R602.3(1)–(4)
Wood structural panel sheathing identification (PS 1/PS 2/CSA O325/O437)

rules.title: Structural insulated panels in wood walls must be manufactured and identified per ANSI/APA PRS 610.1
rules.intent: Ensure SIPs used as wall-framing elements have documented structural performance and a conforming grade mark.
evidence_required: ANSI/APA PRS 610.1 grade mark or certificate of inspection on each panel
Manufacturer data sheet citing ANSI/APA PRS 610.1
Structural notes specifying SIP designation

rules.title: Anchor braced-wall-line sills to concrete or masonry foundations per R403.1.6 and R602.11.1
rules.intent: Provide a continuous load path from the braced wall line into the foundation so wind and seismic shears do not pull the structure off its foundation.
evidence_required: Foundation plan showing anchor bolt size, spacing and embedment per Section R403.1.6
Sill detail with plate washer dimensions where SDC D0/D1/D2 (or SDC C townhouse) applies
Stepped-foundation detail per R602.11.2 if foundation height varies more than 4 ft

rules.title: Use prescriptive cold-formed steel wall framing only within the size, wind, exposure and snow limits of R603.1.1
rules.intent: Bound the prescriptive CFS wall provisions to building geometries and environmental loads the underlying tables actually cover.
evidence_required: Building dimensions on plan within 60 ft x 40 ft envelope
Wind speed (≤140 mph), exposure category and ground snow load called out from Table R301.2
Stories above grade noted on framing plans
If outside limits: AISI S230 design package
Mill certificate / AISI S240 product mark on each member

rules.title: Design and construct masonry per Section R606, TMS 402, TMS 403 or TMS 404; California requires architect/engineer stamping
rules.intent: Route every masonry assembly into a recognized design standard and ensure California-licensed professional review (Business and Professions Code 5537.1 and 6737.1).
evidence_required: Stamped and signed structural drawings from a California-licensed architect or engineer
Reference to TMS 402/403/404 or Section R606 on the design basis sheet
Masonry unit and mortar specifications complying with R606.2

rules.title: Anchor masonry walls to floors and roofs per Figure R606.11(1)–(3); footings may serve as points of lateral support
rules.intent: Provide a positive tie between masonry walls and the diaphragms that brace them, completing the lateral load path.
evidence_required: Connection details at floor and roof matching Figure R606.11(1), (2) or (3) as appropriate to the SDC and wind environment
Anchor schedule with size, embedment and spacing
Diaphragm sheathing/blocking detail per R606.12.1.1 where applicable

rules.title: Apply Section R606.12 seismic provisions to all masonry in SDC D0, D1, D2 (and to townhouses in SDC C)
rules.intent: Trigger the seismic detailing rules for masonry only where the seismic environment requires them, exempting glass unit masonry and veneers governed by their own sections.
evidence_required: Seismic Design Category from Table R301.2 on the title sheet
Cross-reference on plans to applicable subsection (R606.12.2, .3 or .4)
Diaphragm fastener schedule per R606.12.1.1 (4-in OC perimeter where width-to-thickness >2:1)

rules.title: Townhouse masonry in SDC C: provide minimum solid wall length per Table R606.12.2.1 and reinforce per R606.12.2.2/R606.12.2.3
rules.intent: Force townhouses with masonry exterior walls in SDC C to have enough solid wall and minimum reinforcement to resist seismic forces.
evidence_required: Wall elevation showing each qualifying solid wall segment ≥3 ft long and gaps ≤18 ft
Calculation of percent solid wall vs. inscribing rectangle dimension along each direction
Reinforcing schedule for partitions/screen walls per R606.12.2.2.3 and shear walls per R606.12.2.3.3
Connector schedule providing ≥200 plf at ≤4 ft on center to floor and roof

rules.title: Masonry in SDC D0/D1: meet R606.12.2 plus added reinforcement (≥0.002 A_g total, 0.0007 A_g each direction); no AAC in LFRS
rules.intent: Add minimum two-way reinforcement and material restrictions to masonry assemblies that must resist higher seismic demand.
evidence_required: Reinforcing schedule meeting 0.002 total / 0.0007 each-direction ratios per Table R606.12.3.2
Mortar specification confirming Type M or S Portland-cement-lime / mortar cement (no Type N or masonry cement in LFRS)
Lateral tie detail with 135° or 180° standard hook anchorage
Note prohibiting AAC masonry in the lateral force resisting system

rules.title: Masonry in SDC D2: meet D1 plus stricter stack-bond reinforcement (≥0.0015 A_g not in LFRS, ≥0.0025 A_g in LFRS)
rules.intent: Provide the highest-seismic detailing requirements for stack-bond masonry, including tighter spacing and solid grouting.
evidence_required: Reinforcing schedule for stack-bond walls keyed to Tables R606.12.4.1 and R606.12.4.2 with bar size by wall thickness
Specification for solid grouting and use of hollow open-end units or two wythes of solid units
Compliance with all D1 requirements (R606.12.3) by reference

rules.title: Bond multiple-wythe masonry walls by headers, wall ties/joint reinforcement, or natural/cast stone bonders
rules.intent: Make sure facing and backing wythes act compositely and resist out-of-plane loads, with cavity wall geometry kept within tested limits.
evidence_required: Wall section showing wythe thicknesses and cavity dimension
Bonder/header layout or wall-tie schedule meeting R606.13.1, .2 or .3
Calculations supporting any cavity wider than 4 in
Ashlar/rubble bonder layout drawings where natural stone is used

rules.title: Design exterior concrete walls per Section R608, PCA 100, ACI 318 or ACI 332; require California stamped documents
rules.intent: Force concrete-wall designs into a recognized standard and require California-licensed professional sign-off on the construction documents.
evidence_required: Stamped structural drawings naming PCA 100, ACI 318, ACI 332 or Section R608 as the design basis
Concrete wall sections and reinforcement schedules
Mix design submittal per R608.5

rules.title: Use the prescriptive concrete-wall provisions only within the geometric, load, wind and seismic limits of R608.2
rules.intent: Bound the prescriptive concrete-wall path to building configurations the tables actually cover; everything else goes to PCA 100 / ACI 318.
evidence_required: Building dimensions, mean roof height and story count on plans within R608.2 limits
Wind speed, exposure and SDC from Table R301.2 on title sheet
Dead-load calculations for floor/ceiling, roof and overhang
If outside limits: PCA 100 or ACI 318 stamped design package

rules.title: Concrete walls must comply with the shapes and minimum cross-sectional dimensions of Table R608.3
rules.intent: Ensure prescriptive concrete walls have the section properties the design tables assumed.
evidence_required: Wall sections dimensioned to match the shape and thickness in Table R608.3
Note identifying wall type (flat / waffle-grid / screen-grid)
Concrete wall weight calculation for verification against tabulated maximum

rules.title: Flat concrete walls: minimum 4 in nominal thickness and comply with Table R608.3 / Figure R608.3(1)
rules.intent: Set the minimum thickness for flat-formed concrete walls to maintain assumed flexural and shear capacity.
evidence_required: Wall section showing nominal thickness ≥4 in
Plans key sections to Figure R608.3(1)
Construction tolerance note: as-built thickness within −1/2 in to +1/4 in of nominal

rules.title: Waffle-grid concrete walls: minimum 6 in nominal core thickness, comply with Table R608.3 / Figure R608.3(2)
rules.intent: Maintain core dimensions in waffle-grid ICF walls so the prescriptive design assumptions hold.
evidence_required: Wall section keyed to Figure R608.3(2) showing horizontal and vertical core thickness ≥6 in
Manufacturer ICF data sheet listing core W and T compliant with Table R608.3
Wall weight check vs. tabulated maximum

rules.title: Screen-grid concrete walls: minimum 6 in nominal core thickness, comply with Table R608.3 / Figure R608.3(3)
rules.intent: Maintain core dimensions in screen-grid ICF walls so the prescriptive design assumptions hold.
evidence_required: Wall section keyed to Figure R608.3(3) showing core thickness ≥6 in
Manufacturer ICF data sheet listing core dimensions compliant with Table R608.3
Wall weight check vs. tabulated maximum

rules.title: Stay-in-place concrete forms must meet flame-spread, interior-covering, exterior-covering and (for flat ICF) ASTM E2634 requirements
rules.intent: Treat ICF foam not just as a form but as combustible insulation that must be ignition-protected, weather-protected, and conformant to ASTM E2634 for flat systems.
evidence_required: Manufacturer documentation showing surface burning indices per R302.9 / R316.3
Detail of mechanically fastened gypsum board on the interior face of the ICF
Exterior cladding specification for the ICF face
ASTM E2634 listing for flat ICF forms

rules.title: Connect concrete walls to footings, floors, ceilings and roofs per Section R608.9 (and R608.9.2/R608.9.3)
rules.intent: Provide a closed lateral and uplift load path between concrete walls and the diaphragms above and the foundation below.
evidence_required: Connection details at every wall-to-floor, wall-to-ceiling and wall-to-roof interface keyed to Figures R608.9(1)–(12) or to a stamped engineering design
Anchor bolt schedule with embedment, spacing and tension-tie size per the applicable Table R608.9(n)
Specification prohibiting J/L-hook anchor bolts where prescriptive figures are used
Hole-size detail for face-mounted ledger bolts through stay-in-place forms (≥4 in dia or 4 in square)

rules.title: Design SIP walls per Section R610 within the size, wind, snow and seismic limits, with California-stamped documents
rules.intent: Limit prescriptive SIP wall design to building configurations the underlying tables cover and require licensed-professional review under California law.
evidence_required: Stamped structural drawings from a California-licensed architect or engineer
Building plan dimensions and wall heights within R610.2 limits
Wind speed, exposure, ground snow load and SDC from Table R301.2
ANSI/APA PRS 610.1 grade mark or certificate of inspection for each SIP
Connection details per Tables R610.5(1)/(2) and Figures R610.5(1)–(5)

rules.title: Structural stability of evacuation-supporting portions in CVFPP areas
rules.intent: Ensure portions of buildings supporting evacuation locations resist flood-induced flotation, collapse and lateral movement during a 200-year flood event in areas protected by the Central Valley Flood Protection Plan.
evidence_required: Construction documents showing WSEL200 and floor/roof elevations (per AY101.1)
Hydrostatic load calculations per ASCE 7 Chapter 5 referencing depth from WSEL200
Structural drawings of anchorage and load path for evacuation-supporting portions
If using flood vents under exception, drawings showing minimum one vent on two opposite sides per Figure AY103
Registered design professional stamp where automatic-entry openings, valves or yield panels are used

rules.title: Use of defined terms and fallback meanings
rules.intent: Establish that defined terms govern code interpretation and provide an authoritative fallback to the California Building Standards Code (and Webster's for SFM applications) when terms are not defined.
evidence_required: Construction documents and specifications using terms consistent with Chapter 2 definitions
For SFM-regulated occupancies under Section 1.11, references documenting Webster's Third fallback when applicable

rules.title: Complete load path for all prescribed loads
rules.intent: Require buildings to safely support all prescribed loads with a complete load path from origin to foundation so prescriptive construction is presumed compliant.
evidence_required: Structural plans showing continuous load path from roof to foundation
Load schedules listing dead, live, roof, flood, snow, wind and seismic loads applicable to the project
Indication of which prescriptive provisions are being used (or engineered design package per R301.1.3)
Climatic and geographic design criteria filled in per Table R301.2

rules.title: Permitted alternative prescriptive standards to R301
rules.intent: Allow specific industry standards (WFCM, AISI S230, ICC 400) as alternatives to R301 prescriptive provisions, with engineered portions referred to the California Building Code.
evidence_required: Designation of which alternative standard (WFCM, AISI S230, or ICC 400) governs the design
Cross-reference table demonstrating compliance with the chosen standard's limits
If engineering supplements the prescriptive standard, engineered calculations per California Building Code stamped by a California-licensed design professional
Identification of any provisions of this code that still apply to elements outside the chosen standard

rules.title: Engineered design required for elements exceeding prescriptive limits
rules.intent: Require accepted engineering practice (and California-licensed architect/engineer stamp where amended) for any structural element that exceeds R301 prescriptive limits or otherwise does not conform to the code.

california_amendments.statutory_basis: Business and Professions Code Sections 5537 and 6737.1

evidence_required: Engineering calculations and structural drawings stamped by a California-licensed architect or engineer for the nonconforming portion
Identification of which elements exceed R301 prescriptive limits and the basis for engineered design
Demonstration that engineered elements are compatible with the surrounding conventional framing
For woodframe dwellings >2 stories + basement, complete stamped construction documents
For cold-formed steel, concrete, masonry, or SIP buildings, stamped floor/wall/roof-ceiling structural drawings

rules.title: Intermodal shipping containers as buildings
rules.intent: Direct designers of repurposed intermodal shipping containers to the structural provisions of the California Building Code rather than CRC prescriptive provisions.
evidence_required: Structural calculations and drawings demonstrating compliance with CBC Section 3115
Identification of container origin, size, and modification details (cuts, openings, reinforcements)
California-licensed architect or engineer stamp on container structural design
Connection details for stacking, anchorage, and load path to foundation

rules.title: Wind design required where prescriptive wind provisions do not apply
rules.intent: Require an engineered wind design (using one of the listed methods) wherever Figure R301.2.1.1 mandates wind design or where the ultimate design wind speed in a special wind region equals or exceeds 140 mph.

must_use_one_of: ICC Standard for Residential Construction in High-Wind Regions (ICC 600)
ASCE 7 Minimum Design Loads for Buildings and Other Structures
AISI Standard for Cold-Formed Steel Framing - Prescriptive Method (AISI S230)

evidence_required: Identification of ultimate design wind speed Vult and whether the site is in a special wind region
Indication of which Figure R301.2.1.1 region applies
Wind design package using one of the five permitted methods (WFCM, ICC 600, ASCE 7, AISI S230, or CBC)
Stamped calculations by a California-licensed engineer for engineered wind designs
Schedule of components and cladding pressures for wall coverings, windows, doors, garage doors and skylights

rules.title: Protection of openings in windborne debris regions
rules.intent: Require glazed exterior openings in windborne debris regions to be protected against impact and pressure to keep the building envelope intact during high-wind events.

glazing_protection_must_meet: Large Missile Test of ASTM E1886
ASTM E1996 as modified in Section R301.2.1.2.1

evidence_required: Designation that the project site is in a windborne debris region (per Table R301.2 footnote m and Figure R301.2(2))
Test reports showing glazed openings comply with ASTM E1886 (Large Missile) and ASTM E1996
For garage doors with glazing, ANSI/DASMA 115 or approved impact-resistance test report
If wood structural panel exception is used: panel thickness, span, precut/predrilled detail, attachment hardware schedule, and Vult/mean roof height calculations
Component and cladding pressure calculations per Table R301.2.1(1) or ASCE 7

rules.title: Use actual material weights for dead load
rules.intent: Require dead load determination to use actual material weights and account for fixed service equipment so the structure is not under-designed for self-weight.
evidence_required: Dead load schedule listing each assembly (roof, floors, walls, partitions) with material weights
Inventory of fixed service equipment (HVAC units, water heaters, solar arrays, etc.) and their weights included in dead load
Manufacturer data sheets supporting equipment weights
Structural calculations showing dead load values used in member sizing

rules.title: Minimum uniformly distributed live loads
rules.intent: Require structural members to be designed for at least the minimum uniformly distributed live loads in Table R301.5 to ensure adequate occupant and use-load capacity.
evidence_required: Live load schedule per occupancy/use that references Table R301.5 values
Member sizing calculations using the tabulated live loads
Verification of stair tread capacity for the 300-lb concentrated load on a 2x2 area
Verification of elevated garage floor capacity for the 2,000-lb concentrated load on a 4.5x4.5 area
Identification of attic live load category (with or without storage) and corresponding load

rules.title: Under-floor space moisture control
rules.intent: Prevent moisture damage and decay in crawl spaces by requiring either ventilation (R408.2) or unvented-with-controls construction (R408.3), plus access, debris removal, grading, flood resistance and a vapor retarder where applicable.

requires.ventilation_minimum_net_area_ratio: 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft of under-floor area (or 1/1500 with Class I vapor retarder over ground)

evidence_required: Crawl-space ventilation calculation showing net area >= 1/150 (or 1/1500 with Class I vapor retarder) of under-floor area
Plan showing ventilation openings within 3 ft of each external corner (or cross-ventilation layout when vapor retarder is used)
If unvented: Class I vapor retarder spec, mechanical exhaust/conditioned-supply/plenum/dehumidification design
Access opening dimensions on plans (>= 18x24 in floor or 16x24 in wall) and areaway detail where below grade
For flood hazard areas: flood opening details per R322.2.2 and grading sections showing under-floor grade vs outside finished grade

rules.title: Floor construction must accommodate and transmit Section R301 loads
rules.intent: Ensure all floors (including attic-equipment-supporting floors) are designed to carry and transfer R301 loads to the supporting structure.
evidence_required: Floor framing plans with member sizes, spans and spacings
Load takedown showing R301 loads carried by each floor and transferred to supporting walls/beams/foundations
Identification of attic spaces housing mechanical/plumbing equipment with corresponding floor design
Connection details transmitting loads to supporting structural elements

rules.title: Wood floor framing materials must be identified and conform to standards
rules.intent: Ensure wood and wood-based products used for load-supporting floor framing are identifiable, traceable to recognized standards, and of established structural capacity.
evidence_required: Lumber grade marks visible on submitted samples or specified in construction documents
Manufacturer specifications and ICC-ES or equivalent reports for prefabricated I-joists, glulam, SCL, CLT and rim boards
ANSI/APA, ASTM and DOC PS 20 references in the wood material schedule
For preservative-treated members, identification per R317.2
For end-jointed lumber in fire-resistance-rated assemblies, HRA designation in grade mark

rules.title: Draftstopping required in floor assemblies
rules.intent: Require draftstopping in floor framing per R302.12 to limit concealed-space air movement that could spread fire or smoke.
evidence_required: Floor framing plans showing draftstop locations and continuity per R302.12
Specification of draftstop materials (e.g., 1/2-in gypsum, 3/8-in wood structural panel, or other approved materials) per R302.12
Section details showing draftstop full-depth integration with framing
Coordination with fireblocking per R502.13/R302.11 at penetrations

rules.title: Windborne debris protection of windows, glass doors and doors with glass
rules.intent: Require fenestration in windborne debris regions to be protected by tested-and-labeled assemblies or impact-protective systems so the building envelope remains intact during high-wind events.

impact_protective_systems.design_wind_pressure_basis: Table R301.2.1(1) adjusted by Table R301.2.1(2) or ASCE 7 (with optional 0.6 multiplier when ASCE 7 used)

evidence_required: Test reports for fenestration to ASTM E1886 + ASTM E1996 (or AAMA 506) from approved independent laboratory
Labels on installed fenestration showing manufacturer, performance characteristics, and approved inspection agency
For impact protective systems: ASTM E1886/E1996 impact reports plus ASTM E330 design wind pressure reports
Design wind pressure calculations per Table R301.2.1(1) adjusted by R301.2.1(2) or per ASCE 7 (with 0.6 multiplier documentation if used)
Permanent (non-removable) label evidence on impact protective systems

rules.title: Solar energy systems comply with Section R324
rules.intent: Establishes the scope: any solar energy system installed on a one- or two-family dwelling falls under Section R324.
evidence_required: Identification of the solar energy system type on plans (PV, BIPV, solar thermal)
Reference on plans to Section R324 compliance

rules.title: PV systems designed and installed per R324.3.1-R324.7.1, manufacturer instructions, and CA Electrical Code
rules.intent: Ensures PV systems follow the specific PV subsections, the manufacturer's installation instructions, and the California Electrical Code for electrical work.
evidence_required: Manufacturer's installation instructions submitted with the plan set
Electrical plans stamped or noted as compliant with California Electrical Code
PV system layout drawing referencing R324.3 through R324.7

rules.title: PV panels, modules, inverters, and mounting systems must be listed and labeled
rules.intent: Ensures all PV equipment carries the proper safety listings so it has been independently tested for fire, electrical, and mounting safety.
evidence_required: Cut sheets / spec sheets for PV modules showing UL 1703 or UL 61730-1/-2 listing marks
Inverter cut sheet showing UL 1741 listing and, if grid-tied, utility-interaction listing
Mounting system cut sheet showing UL 2703 listing
Manufacturer installation instructions for the mounting system

rules.title: Rooftop PV systems and their supporting roofs designed for applicable gravity loads
rules.intent: Ensures both the PV array structure and the roof underneath can carry the weight and gravity loads that come with adding PV.
evidence_required: Structural calculations for the PV racking/support system signed by a licensed engineer
Roof framing calculations or analysis demonstrating capacity to carry added PV dead load
Plan note referencing Chapter 3 (gravity loads) and Chapter 8 (roof-ceiling construction)

rules.title: Roof load cases for portions covered and not covered by PV
rules.intent: Defines the specific load combinations the roof must be designed for so PV addition does not under-stress areas with PV (snow case) or leave bare areas under-designed for live/snow load.
evidence_required: Structural calculations showing both load cases for PV-covered roof areas
Structural calculations showing dead + roof live/snow for non-PV-covered roof areas
Reference to Table R301.2 climatic snow load on plans

rules.title: Rooftop PV designed for component-and-cladding wind loads
rules.intent: Ensures rooftop PV panels and supports resist wind uplift using component-and-cladding pressures, adjusted for site height and exposure.
evidence_required: Wind-load calculations for the PV array using Table R301.2.1(1) C&C loads
Site exposure category and mean roof height documented in calculations
Attachment / anchor capacity calculations stamped by an engineer

rules.title: BIPV systems serving as roof covering installed per Section R905
rules.intent: Treats BIPV products that act as roofing the same as any other roof covering for installation purposes.
evidence_required: Roof plan identifying BIPV product as the roof covering
Reference on plans to Section R905 compliance for the BIPV product

rules.title: Photovoltaic shingles comply with R905.16
rules.intent: Routes PV shingle installation to the dedicated shingle requirements (deck, slope, underlayment, listing, attachment, wind).
evidence_required: Roof plan identifying PV shingles as roof covering
Reference on plans to Section R905.16

rules.title: BIPV systems must have fire classification per R902.3
rules.intent: Ensures BIPV products carry a roof-covering fire class (A, B or C) so they meet the same fire performance as a conventional roof covering.
evidence_required: BIPV product listing/label showing UL 7103 fire classification (Class A, B, or C)
Plan note specifying required fire class for the project (per R902.1.1/R902.1.2)

rules.title: BIPV roof panels comply with R905.17
rules.intent: Routes BIPV roof panel installation to the dedicated section covering deck, slope, underlayment, ice barrier, material standards, and attachment.
evidence_required: Roof plan identifying BIPV roof panels as the roof covering
Reference on plans to Section R905.17

rules.title: Ground-mounted PV systems designed and installed per Section R301
rules.intent: Applies the general structural design provisions of Section R301 to ground-mounted PV arrays so they resist gravity, wind, and seismic loads.
evidence_required: Site plan showing the ground-mounted array location and a minimum 10-foot clear, brush-free perimeter
Structural calculations for the ground-mount foundation/support per Section R301
Documentation of fire-separation distance from the enforcing agency

rules.title: Elevated PV support structures comply with R324.8.1 or R324.8.2
rules.intent: Captures the scope choice for elevated PV support structures (carports, trellises, canopies) between two compliance paths based on the deck/roof beneath.
evidence_required: Plan note identifying the chosen compliance path (R324.8.1 or R324.8.2)
Cross-section or detail showing whether the deck below the PV is open grid/noncombustible or a roof assembly

rules.title: Elevated PV over open grid framing or noncombustible deck must use fire-rated PV panels
rules.intent: Bans 'not fire rated' modules in elevated structures that lack a fire-resistive roof beneath, where the PV panel itself is the fire barrier.
evidence_required: PV module listing/label showing UL 1703 (or UL 61730-1 + 61730-2) fire type rating
Plan note prohibiting use of modules marked 'not fire rated'
Detail showing the open grid framing or noncombustible deck below the panels

rules.title: Elevated PV installed over a roof assembly fire-classified per R324.4
rules.intent: When the elevated PV sits over a real roof assembly, the system is treated as rooftop-mounted PV for fire classification purposes.
evidence_required: PV system fire-classification documentation matching the roof assembly required class
Cross-section showing PV elevated above an existing roof assembly

rules.title: Continuous water-resistive barrier behind exterior wall veneer
rules.intent: Ensures liquid water that gets past the cladding has a continuous drainage plane back out of the wall assembly.
evidence_required: Specification of the WRB material with ASTM compliance noted on the wall section/details
Wall section showing continuous WRB to top of wall and around penetrations
Detail showing 2-inch minimum horizontal lap and 6-inch minimum joint lap (felt or ASTM E2556)
Flashing details at openings keyed to Section R703.4

rules.title: Roof assembly design, materials, construction and quality governed by Chapter 9
rules.intent: Establishes that any roof assembly on a one- or two-family dwelling falls under Chapter 9 for design, materials, construction, and quality.
evidence_required: Roof plan and details on the construction documents
Specification of roof covering type and roof assembly components

rules.title: BIPV products as roof covering: tested, listed, and labeled to UL 7103
rules.intent: California amendment requiring BIPV products acting as roof covering to be fire-classified to UL 7103, with mandatory installation of Class A/B/C BIPV near a lot line.
evidence_required: BIPV product UL 7103 listing/label documentation
Site plan dimensioning the closest roof edge to lot lines
Plan note declaring fire class (A, B or C) of the BIPV product

rules.title: Rooftop-mounted PV systems: tested and identified to UL 2703
rules.intent: Requires rooftop-mounted PV (mounted on or above the roof covering) to carry a UL 2703 fire-classification listing and to be installed per the listing.
evidence_required: PV system UL 2703 listing/label and fire-classification documentation
Manufacturer installation instructions consistent with the listing
Site plan dimensioning roof edge to lot lines
Plan note declaring jurisdictional fire class requirement, if any

rules.title: Roof decks covered with approved roof coverings; flashings, coping, and drainage installed
rules.intent: Ensures the roof assembly keeps water out of the building through approved coverings, flashings at intersections and penetrations, parapet copings, and proper drainage.
evidence_required: Roof covering specification (approved type per R905)
Flashing details at parapet walls, sidewalls, eave-to-sidewall, and roof penetrations
Cricket/saddle detail for any chimney or penetration wider than 30 inches
Coping detail for parapet walls
Drainage plan with low-point drains and overflow drains/scuppers per R903.4.1

rules.title: Roof covering materials compatible, conform to standards, and bear identifying marks
rules.intent: Quality-control requirements: roof materials must be compatible, meet referenced standards, and arrive at the site in identifiable, labeled packaging.
evidence_required: Specification listing roof covering material and applicable ASTM/UL standard
Submittal of cut sheets / labels showing compliance and testing agency
Compatibility statement for combined materials in the roof assembly

rules.title: Roof coverings installed per applicable subsections of R905 and manufacturer instructions
rules.intent: Establishes Section R905 as the controlling section for the installation of every type of roof covering, including the requirement to resist component-and-cladding wind loads.
evidence_required: Plan reference to specific R905 subsection for the chosen roof covering
Manufacturer installation instructions on the submittal
Component-and-cladding wind pressure values used in the design

rules.title: Underlayment for listed roof coverings conforms to standards and is applied/attached per R905.1.1 tables
rules.intent: Requires the underlayment beneath shingles, tile, metal, slate, wood, and PV shingles to meet a recognized standard and be installed and fastened per the prescriptive tables.
evidence_required: Underlayment product spec sheet showing ASTM D226 / D1970 / D4869 / D6757 compliance label
Roof detail showing underlayment lap pattern per Table R905.1.1(2)
Fastening schedule for the underlayment per Table R905.1.1(3)
If using a R905.1.1 exception, the alternative product data and installation method documented

rules.title: Photovoltaic shingles: deck, slope, underlayment, listing, attachment, and wind resistance
rules.intent: Provides the full prescriptive package for installing PV shingles as the roof covering, paralleling other shingle products plus a UL listing for the PV product itself.
evidence_required: Roof framing detail showing solid or closely-fitted deck
Roof plan or section confirming slope is 2:12 or greater
Underlayment specification per R905.1.1 and ice barrier per R905.1.2 if applicable
PV shingle UL 7103 (or UL 61730-1 + UL 61730-2) listing/label
Manufacturer attachment schedule and Table R905.16.6 wind classification matched to site Vult

rules.title: Radon control appendix applicability scope
rules.intent: Trigger radon-resistant construction provisions only where the appendix has been adopted by the jurisdiction or where the project is in an EPA Zone 1 county.
evidence_required: Cover-sheet note identifying jurisdiction's adoption of Appendix AF or project county designation as EPA Radon Zone 1
Reference to Figure AF101.1 / Table AF101.1 with project county highlighted

rules.title: Apply radon-resistant construction in adopted/Zone 1 jurisdictions
rules.intent: Limit AF103/AF104 radon construction and testing requirements to new construction where radon resistance is required by the local jurisdiction.
evidence_required: Building official determination letter or ordinance citation invoking Appendix AF
Site information identifying county and Zone 1 status

rules.title: Radon-resistant construction package for new dwellings
rules.intent: Pre-install gas-permeable subfloor, soil-gas-retarder, sealed entry routes, passive vent pipe, and electrical rough-in so the dwelling can resist and, if needed, mitigate radon entry.
evidence_required: Foundation/slab section detail showing gas-permeable layer thickness, gradation, and 6-mil soil-gas-retarder with lap dimensions
Schedule of sealed penetrations, joints, sumps, and dampproofing per AF103.4 with sealant specifications
Plumbing/mechanical drawings showing passive vent pipe diameter, routing, roof termination clearances, and label locations
Electrical drawings showing future radon fan circuit terminated in approved box at attic/anticipated fan location
Manufacturer cut sheet for any factory-sealed crawl-space air handler used to claim AF103.4.7 exception

rules.title: Radon testing protocol and 4 pCi/L mitigation threshold
rules.intent: Verify radon-resistant construction performs within the EPA action level (<4 pCi/L) by prescribing test conditions, testers, duration, and corrective actions when the level is exceeded.
evidence_required: Written radon test report stamped by tester showing location, duration, device, and pCi/L result
Closure log documenting >=12 hours of closed-house conditions prior to testing
If average >= 4 pCi/L: post-mitigation retest report demonstrating result < 4 pCi/L
Documentation that test was performed after blower-door test and with HVAC (and any installed radon fan) operating

rules.title: Existing-building work classification scope
rules.intent: Classify any work in legally existing buildings into repair, renovation, alteration, or reconstruction so the appropriate stringency of provisions applies.
evidence_required: Permit application classifying the scope of work as repair/renovation/alteration/reconstruction
Work-area drawings keyed to category designations

rules.title: Existing-building work shall not reduce safety or compliance
rules.intent: Ensure that any repair/renovation/alteration/reconstruction does not make the structure unsafe or less code-compliant than before the work was undertaken.
evidence_required: Statement from engineer of record that the work does not create or increase nonconformity
Comparison narrative of pre/post-work compliance status for affected systems
If invoking CEBC equivalence: cross-reference to applicable CEBC sections

rules.title: Replacement window energy, safety glazing, EERO, and fall-prevention requirements
rules.intent: When existing windows or safety glazing are replaced, ensure the replacement meets current energy, safety glazing, emergency-escape, and fall-prevention rules without imposing a structural reframe.
evidence_required: NFRC label and energy compliance documentation for each replacement window
Hazardous-location plan showing safety-glazing locations per R308
EERO window schedule with manufacturer's largest standard size sized to existing rough opening
ASTM F2090 listing/certification for window opening control or fall prevention devices
Sill-height/grade-elevation detail demonstrating fall-prevention trigger evaluation

rules.title: Smoke alarms and flood-hazard provisions trigger regardless of work category
rules.intent: Bring existing dwellings up to current smoke-alarm requirements when work is performed and ensure work in flood hazard areas is processed under R105.3.1.1.
evidence_required: Smoke alarm plan showing units installed per R314.2.2 in all required locations
Flood hazard determination per Table R301.2 with permit routed under R105.3.1.1 if applicable
Elevation certificate or flood vent details when work is in a flood hazard area

rules.title: Tiny-house appendix scope
rules.intent: Apply tiny-house relaxations only to single dwelling units that are 400 sq ft or less (excluding lofts) where the appendix has been adopted.
evidence_required: Floor-area calculation excluding lofts on cover sheet
Use designation as single dwelling unit

rules.title: Tiny-house emergency escape and rescue, including egress roof access windows in lofts
rules.intent: Require tiny houses to meet R310 EERO rules while explicitly allowing egress roof access windows in sleeping lofts when sized and placed within reach.
evidence_required: EERO schedule showing each sleeping room compliance with R310
Section detail showing egress roof access window with bottom of opening dimension to loft floor
Manufacturer specification for skylight/roof window confirming R310.2.1 net clear opening area

rules.title: Tiny-house air leakage, mechanical ventilation, and alternative energy compliance
rules.intent: Cap envelope leakage at 0.30 cfm50 per sf of enclosure, require whole-house mechanical ventilation, and provide an alternative path to Chapter 11 / Energy Code compliance for tiny houses.
evidence_required: Blower-door test report showing leakage <= 0.30 cfm50 per sf of enclosure area, with enclosure area calculation
M1505.4 whole-house mechanical ventilation schedule and fan specifications
Insulation and fenestration schedule referenced to Table N1102.1.2
Renewable energy production calculation demonstrating >=90% of total and DHW energy if claiming alternative compliance
Lighting compliance documentation per N1104

rules.title: Light straw-clay wall thermal classification and R-value
rules.intent: Classify dense (>=20 pcf) light straw-clay infill as a mass wall and lower-density (<20 pcf) infill as wood-frame for code R-value purposes, using the R-values from Table AR103.2.3.
evidence_required: Wall assembly schedule listing light straw-clay density (pcf) for each wall type
R-value calculation sheet demonstrating compliance with the applicable column of Table N1102.1.3
Reference to Table AR103.2.3 for the assigned thermal resistance per inch

rules.title: Central Valley Flood Protection Plan area scope
rules.intent: Apply Appendix AY to new construction, change of use, repair, and substantial improvement/restoration in CVFPP-protected areas where 200-year flood depth is anticipated to exceed 3 ft.
evidence_required: Site map showing project parcel within CVFPP area per DWR data (water.ca.gov/BuildingCodes)
Construction documents listing WSEL200 and floor/roof elevations
Health & Safety Code 50465 area determination

rules.title: Evacuation location and route required in CVFPP areas
rules.intent: Provide an evacuation location at least one foot above WSEL200 with an unobstructed route so occupants below the 200-year flood level can shelter and be rescued.
evidence_required: Plan showing evacuation location with finished floor elevation > WSEL200 + 1 ft
Occupant-load calculation including portions below WSEL200 and area calculation at 7 sf/occupant
Egress path drawing showing doors openable without keys/tools
Means of escape detail (R310-compliant window, R311 exterior door, rooftop stair/ramp/ladder, etc.)
Hydrostatic load calculation per ASCE 7 Chapter 5 supporting evacuation-supporting structure design

rules.title: Emergency housing appendix scope
rules.intent: Apply Appendix AZ to emergency sleeping cabins, emergency transportable housing units, membrane structures and tents only when occupied during a declared state/local emergency or shelter crisis.
evidence_required: Copy of formal declaration of state/local emergency or shelter crisis citing Gov. Code 8558 or 8698
Site plan listing structure types deployed (cabins, ETHUs, tents, membrane structures)
Enforcing agency authorization letter where exceptions are claimed

rules.title: Emergency sleeping cabin construction, egress, electrical, and life-safety requirements
rules.intent: Set minimum floor area, structural live loads, ceiling heights, two remote egress paths, electrical service, and smoke/CO alarms for relocatable hard-sided emergency sleeping cabins.
evidence_required: Floor plan with interior area calculation and occupant-count-based area schedule
Structural calcs documenting floor (40 psf), wall/roof (15 psf), and roof (20 psf) live loads (or higher snow load if applicable)
Section drawings showing 80 in habitable and 76 in bath/kitchen ceiling heights
Egress plan showing two remote egress paths and an egress window meeting AZ104.4.1 dimensions
Electrical riser/plan showing continuous power, interior lighting, listed heating equipment with dedicated outlet, and GFCI receptacle
Smoke alarm and (if applicable) carbon monoxide alarm plan referencing R314/R315

rules.title: Emergency transportable housing units must comply with HSC Div. 13 and Title 25
rules.intent: Defer construction standards for manufactured homes, mobilehomes, multifamily manufactured homes, commercial modulars, recreational vehicles, and park trailers used as emergency housing to existing California state housing law.
evidence_required: HCD insignia or certification label for each unit (manufactured home, mobilehome, multifamily MH, park trailer, RV, or commercial modular)
Documentation of compliance with HSC Division 13 Part 2 and Title 25 Division 1 Chapter 3 Subchapter 2
Enforcing agency approval letter for any commercial modular used as ETHU

rules.title: Flood-hazard permit review for work in flood hazard areas
rules.intent: Route any work performed in existing buildings located in a flood hazard area through the special permit-review provisions of R105.3.1.1.
evidence_required: Flood hazard determination per Table R301.2 with FEMA panel reference
Permit application package routed through flood-hazard plan review under R105.3.1.1
Elevation certificate or equivalent documentation

rules.title: Replacement glazing in hazardous locations shall be safety glazing
rules.intent: Ensure that whenever an existing window or glazing is replaced, the replacement glazing in hazardous locations is rated as safety glazing under R308.
evidence_required: Glazing schedule indicating each hazardous location and the corresponding safety-glazing label/rating
Manufacturer certification of safety glazing for replacement panes/sashes

rules.title: Emergency escape and rescue openings required in sleeping rooms
rules.intent: Ensure each sleeping room and basement is served by an emergency escape and rescue opening that meets R310 minimum size, sill height, and operability so occupants can escape and rescuers can enter.
evidence_required: EERO schedule for each sleeping room with net clear opening dimensions and sill height
Window opening control / fall prevention documentation per ASTM F2090 where applicable
Manufacturer specifications confirming R310.2.1 minimum opening area

rules.title: Smoke alarms required regardless of work category and in emergency sleeping cabins
rules.intent: Provide working smoke alarms in existing dwellings whenever work is performed and in every emergency sleeping cabin so occupants are warned of fire.
evidence_required: Smoke alarm location plan referenced to R314.3 (each sleeping room, outside sleeping rooms, on each story)
Listed-product cut sheets or model numbers complying with R314
Interconnection and power source documentation

rules.title: Carbon monoxide alarms required where fuel-burning appliances or fireplaces are present
rules.intent: Detect carbon monoxide in dwelling units that contain fuel-burning appliances or fireplaces, including emergency sleeping cabins.
evidence_required: Mechanical/fireplace plans identifying fuel-burning appliances and fireplaces
CO alarm location plan referenced to R315 with listed-product cut sheets
Power source and interconnection documentation

rules.title: Below-grade concrete and masonry walls shall be dampproofed
rules.intent: Dampproof exterior surfaces of below-grade concrete and masonry block walls to limit water and soil-gas entry, including in radon-resistant assemblies.
evidence_required: Foundation wall section detail showing dampproofing material, application method, and extent below grade
Manufacturer product data sheet for the dampproofing material
